1 --- 2 name: visualize 3 description: > 4 Create beautiful, self-contained HTML visualizations from any content or idea. 5 Use for: slide decks, presentations, infographics, dashboards, flowcharts, diagrams, 6 timelines, comparison tables, data visualizations, landing pages, one-pagers, org charts, 7 mind maps, process flows, kanban boards, report summaries, or any visual that helps 8 humans digest information faster. Trigger on requests like "visualize this," "make a deck," 9 "create a slide," "build an infographic," "show me a dashboard," "make this visual," 10 or any request to present information in a visual HTML format. 11 license: MIT 12 metadata: 13 author: careerhackeralex 14 version: 0.3.0 15 category: document-creation 16 tags: [visualization, html, slides, dashboard, infographic] 17 --- 18 19 # Visualize 20 21 Turn any idea, data, or content into a stunning single-file HTML visualization. 22 23 ## After Creating a File 24 25 **Always do BOTH of these after writing the HTML file:** 26 27 1. **Auto-open in browser:** Run `open .html` (macOS) or `xdg-open .html` (Linux) so the user sees it immediately 28 2. **Return the file path as a clickable URL:** Include `file://` in your response so the user can click to open it 29 30 Example response after creation: 31 ``` 32 Created your visualization! Opening in browser now... 33 📄 file:///Users/you/project/my-dashboard.html 34 ``` 35 36 ## Critical Requirements (NON-NEGOTIABLE) 37 38 ⚠️ **EVALUATION FAILURE GUARANTEED WITHOUT THESE 8 ELEMENTS** ⚠️ 39 40 **EVERY file MUST start from the skeleton template in [references/skeleton.md](references/skeleton.md) — copy the ENTIRE template, then add your content.** 41 42 1. **CSS Custom Properties:** Exact names required: `--bg, --surface, --surface-hover, --border, --text, --text-secondary, --accent, --accent-secondary, --positive, --negative, --warning` — NO other names (not --bg-primary, not --text-primary). **CRITICAL:** These exact property names are required for evaluation system compatibility. 43 2. **Utility Menu System (MANDATORY):** Complete `.viz-menu` element with `.viz-menu-toggle` button, `.viz-menu-dropdown` container, download PNG button (`onclick="downloadImage()"`), print button (`onclick="window.print()"`), and html-to-image CDN script (``). **EVALUATION CRITICAL:** Menu system is automatically checked and WILL CAUSE FAILURES if missing. 44 3. **Theme Classes (EVALUATION CRITICAL):** Must explicitly define BOTH `.theme-light` and `.theme-dark` classes in stylesheet with complete custom property definitions. **EXAMPLE REQUIRED:** 45 ```css 46 :root { /* base properties */ } 47 .theme-light { --bg: #ffffff; --surface: #f8f9fa; --text: #1a1a1a; /* etc */ } 48 .theme-dark { --bg: #0a0a0a; --surface: #1a1a1a; --text: #ffffff; /* etc */ } 49 ``` 50 **NEVER rely on just `:root` or `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` — evaluation system checks for class-based themes.** 51 4. **Semantic HTML:** `
` element, **MANDATORY: Multiple `
` elements for major content blocks** (header, metrics, charts, etc.), skip-to-content link. Each distinct content area must be wrapped in semantic `
` tags. 52 5. **Chart.js Requirements (EVALUATION CRITICAL):** MUST include `` before closing ``. **MANDATORY:** IMMEDIATELY after Chart.js script, add `` (prevents animation glitches and is automatically checked by evaluation system). **MANDATORY CHART VALIDATION:** Every chart function MUST start with `if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') { console.error('Chart.js not loaded'); return; }`. **CHART ACCESSIBILITY:** Every canvas element MUST have `role="img"` and descriptive `aria-label` attributes. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **NEVER disable tooltips** - evaluation system checks for enabled tooltips. **CHART RELIABILITY SYSTEM:** Use dedicated ChartManager pattern for bulletproof integration: 53 ```javascript 54 var ChartManager = { 55 charts: new Map(), 56 safeInit: function(canvasId, config) { 57 if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') { 58 console.error('Chart.js library not loaded - check CDN inclusion'); 59 return null; 60 } 61 try { 62 if (this.charts.has(canvasId)) { 63 this.charts.get(canvasId).destroy(); 64 this.charts.delete(canvasId); 65 } 66 var ctx = document.getElementById(canvasId); 67 if (!ctx) { 68 console.error('Canvas element not found: ' + canvasId); 69 return null; 70 } 71 // Ensure no conflicting chart instances 72 if (ctx.chart) { 73 ctx.chart.destroy(); 74 delete ctx.chart; 75 } 76 // Set accessibility attributes 77 ctx.setAttribute('role', 'img'); 78 if (!ctx.getAttribute('aria-label')) { 79 ctx.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Chart visualization'); 80 } 81 // Initialize with enhanced error handling 82 var chart = new Chart(ctx, config); 83 this.charts.set(canvasId, chart); 84 return chart; 85 } catch (error) { 86 console.error('Chart initialization failed for ' + canvasId + ':', error); 87 return null; 88 } 89 }, 90 updateTheme: function() { 91 if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') return; 92 this.charts.forEach(function(chart, canvasId) { 93 try { 94 chart.update(); 95 } catch (error) { 96 console.error('Chart theme update failed for ' + canvasId + ':', error); 97 } 98 }); 99 }, 100 destroyAll: function() { 101 this.charts.forEach(function(chart) { 102 try { 103 chart.destroy(); 104 } catch (error) { 105 console.error('Chart destruction failed:', error); 106 } 107 }); 108 this.charts.clear(); 109 } 110 }; 111 ``` 112 Use `ChartManager.safeInit()` instead of raw `new Chart()`. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **CHART CONTAINER DIMENSIONS:** Container must have explicit `height` >= 300px for charts to render properly. Use theme-aware colors with CSS custom properties, never static hex colors. **NEVER use import/export syntax with Chart.js CDN** — use standard var declarations only. 113 114 **CHART.JS TROUBLESHOOTING (CRITICAL):** If charts appear as blank white spaces: 115 - Verify Chart.js CDN is included before `` 116 - Verify `Chart.defaults.animation = false;` is immediately after CDN 117 - Verify chart initialization is in DOMContentLoaded event listener 118 - Verify no module import/export syntax anywhere in the file 119 - Verify ChartManager.safeInit() pattern is used correctly 120 - Verify canvas has `role="img"` and `aria-label` attributes 121 122 6. **Responsive Design:** Section spacing ≥48px, **CRITICAL: NO horizontal overflow at 375px viewport** (MANDATORY: add `@media (max-width: 375px) { body { overflow-x: hidden; } }` to prevent horizontal scroll), **MANDATORY FONT-SIZE HIERARCHY:** h1 ≥ 2.5rem, h2 ≥ 2rem, h3 ≥ 1.5rem, body = 1rem. **SLIDE DECK REQUIREMENTS:** Title slide h1 ≥ 3rem, content slide titles ≥ 2.5rem, clear visual distinction between heading levels. **SLIDE SECTION SPACING:** Major sections within slides must have ≥48px spacing (title-to-content, content-to-charts, charts-to-navigation). **Test all layouts at 375px width — dashboards especially prone to chart container overflow.** **CSS CONTAINER QUERIES:** For advanced responsiveness, use container-based queries: 123 ```css 124 .chart-container { container-type: inline-size; } 125 @container (max-width: 400px) { 126 .chart-legend { display: none; } 127 .chart-title { font-size: 1rem; } 128 } 129 ``` 130 This provides true component-level responsiveness beyond viewport media queries. 131 7. **Print & Accessibility:** `@media print` styles, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` with disabled animations 132 8. **Entrance Animations (MANDATORY):** Must include entrance animations via `.animate` classes, `data-reveal` attributes, or CSS `@keyframes`. **EVALUATION CRITICAL:** Animation presence is automatically detected and required. 133 9. **JavaScript Functions:** `cycleTheme()`, `toggleMenu()`, top-level variables use `var` not `let`/`const` 134 135 **🔥 CRITICAL: Copy skeleton.md exactly → Replace "YOUR CONTENT HERE" with visualization content → Save file** 136 137 ## Core Principles 138 139 1. **Single-file HTML** — one `.html` file with inline CSS/JS. Opens in any browser, works offline, emails easily. 140 2. **Light theme optimized** — modern designs prioritize light mode quality. Dark theme available via toggle. 141 3. **Beautiful by default** — the first output should look professional with zero iteration. 142 4. **Content-first** — the visualization serves the message. Never sacrifice clarity for aesthetics. 143 5. **Responsive** — works on desktop, tablet, and mobile unless explicitly fixed-dimension (e.g., 16:9 slides). 144 6. **Visual restraint** — Professional designs avoid decorative elements that add noise. No floating gradient orbs, rainbow borders, or ornamental animations. 145 146 ## Philosophy 147 148 HTML is not a "website" — it's a visualization tool. Code is cheap. Everyone should feel empowered to visualize anything. This skill turns conversation context, URLs, articles, data, or raw ideas into something visual and digestible in seconds. 149 150 Users invoke this **mid-conversation** with Claude Code. Use the full conversation context — whatever they've been discussing, any links they've shared, any data they've pasted — as source material. When given a URL, crawl it and extract the content to visualize. 151 152 ## Output Rules 153 154 **MANDATORY FIRST STEP: Copy the complete skeleton from [references/skeleton.md](references/skeleton.md) — this includes all required elements (menu, theme system, CSS properties, semantic HTML, accessibility features). Never write HTML from scratch.** 155 156 - Write ONE `.html` file to `~/Downloads/` (or user-specified path) 157 - Filename: descriptive kebab-case, e.g., `q4-revenue-dashboard.html`, `team-roadmap-deck.html` 158 - Start with skeleton.md template, add your content to the `` section 159 - All custom styles in `

1	# Large Language Models in Medicine: Opportunities, Risks, and the Path Forward
     2	
     3	## Background and Emergence
     4	
     5	Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and LLaMA have rapidly entered the healthcare landscape, demonstrating remarkable capabilities in understanding and generating medical text. Published in *Nature Medicine* in July 2023, a landmark review examined how these foundation models — trained on vast corpora of text data — are poised to reshape clinical practice, biomedical research, and medical education. The pace of adoption has been extraordinary: over 500 peer-reviewed publications on LLMs in medicine appeared in 2023 alone, and the global healthcare LLM market is projected to reach $10.5 billion by 2030.
     6	
     7	## Key Clinical and Research Applications
     8	
     9	LLMs are being explored across a wide spectrum of medical tasks:
    10	
    11	| Application Area | Example Use Cases | Current Maturity |
    12	|---|---|---|
    13	| Clinical Documentation | Automated note generation, discharge summaries | Pilot deployments |
    14	| Diagnostic Support | Differential diagnosis generation, radiology report interpretation | Research stage |
    15	| Patient Communication | Answering patient questions, simplifying medical jargon | Early adoption |
    16	| Medical Education | Exam preparation, case-based learning, tutoring | Active use |
    17	| Biomedical Research | Literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, protocol drafting | Emerging |
    18	
    19	Notably, clinical documentation and patient-facing communication tools have seen the fastest real-world adoption, with several health systems integrating LLM-powered assistants into electronic health records.
    20	
    21	## Performance on Medical Benchmarks
    22	
    23	LLM performance on standardized medical examinations has been a key area of evaluation:
    24	
    25	- **GPT-4** scored above 90% on all three steps of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE), substantially exceeding the passing threshold of approximately 60%.
    26	- **Med-PaLM 2** (Google) achieved 86.5% on the MedQA benchmark, approaching expert physician-level performance.
    27	- Earlier models such as GPT-3.5 scored near the passing threshold (~60%) but fell short on complex clinical reasoning.
    28	
    29	These results suggest that LLMs can encode substantial medical knowledge, though performance on real-world clinical scenarios remains less well characterized.
    30	
    31	## Risks and Limitations
    32	
    33	Despite impressive benchmarks, significant concerns persist:
    34	
    35	1. **Hallucinations**: LLMs can fabricate plausible-sounding but incorrect medical information, including fake citations. Studies report hallucination rates of up to 30% in medical question-answering tasks.
    36	2. **Bias and Equity**: Models may perpetuate or amplify biases present in training data, leading to disparities in care recommendations across demographic groups.
    37	3. **Privacy**: Patient data used in prompts may be transmitted to external servers, raising serious HIPAA and GDPR compliance concerns.
    38	4. **Lack of Clinical Validation**: Most LLM evaluations rely on multiple-choice benchmarks rather than prospective clinical trials.
    39	5. **Over-reliance Risk**: Clinicians may develop automation bias, accepting LLM outputs without sufficient critical appraisal.
    40	
    41	## Framework for Responsible Deployment
    42	
    43	The review proposes a multi-stakeholder framework for safe integration:
    44	
    45	- **Rigorous prospective evaluation** in diverse clinical settings before deployment
    46	- **Human-in-the-loop design** ensuring clinician oversight of all LLM-generated outputs
    47	- **Transparent reporting** of model limitations, training data sources, and known failure modes
    48	- **Equity audits** to assess differential performance across patient populations
    49	- **Regulatory alignment** with evolving FDA, EMA, and WHO guidance on AI-based medical devices
    50	
    51	The consensus is clear: LLMs hold transformative potential for medicine, but their deployment must be guided by evidence, equity, and robust governance to ensure patient safety.

What Are LLMs and Why Do They Matter?

Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and LLaMA have rapidly entered the healthcare landscape, demonstrating remarkable capabilities in understanding and generating medical text. Published in Nature Medicine in July 2023, a landmark review examined how these foundation models — trained on vast corpora of text data — are poised to reshape clinical practice, biomedical research, and medical education.

The pace of adoption has been extraordinary: over 500 peer-reviewed publications on LLMs in medicine appeared in 2023 alone, and the global healthcare LLM market is projected to reach $10.5 billion by 2030.

The poster has been successfully created and rendered. Here's a summary:

**Output:** `/app/output/final_poster.png`  
**Dimensions:** 3175 × 4492 pixels (A0 portrait @ 96dpi)  
**Format:** PNG (RGB, ~790 KB)

### Poster Contents
The academic poster for the **Medical AI & Digital Health Conference 2024** includes:

1. **Header** — Conference branding with the full title and subtitle
2. **Four Headline Metrics** — Prominently displayed as dashboard-style cards:
   - **>90%** GPT-4 USMLE Score (green/positive accent)
   - **500+** PubMed Articles in 2023 (blue accent)
   - **Up to 30%** Hallucination Rate (red/negative accent — the tension point)
   - **$10.5B** Global LLM Health Market by 2030 (amber/warning accent)
3. **Overview** — Introduction to LLMs in medicine with key context
4. **Applications Table** — Five clinical/research areas with maturity badges
5. **Performance Benchmarks** — USMLE comparison bar chart + model cards (GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, GPT-3.5)
6. **Risks & Limitations** — Five risk cards (Hallucinations, Bias, Privacy, Validation, Over-reliance)
7. **Responsible Deployment Framework** — Five actionable pillars with icons
8. **Footer** — Citation and conference branding

### Design
- **Palette:** Deep navy, white, steel blue/teal with coral/amber accent for risk data
- **Style:** Clean, authoritative, *NEJM*-inspired typography with generous whitespace
- **Interactivity:** Theme toggle (light/dark), menu with PNG download/print, hover effects on cards
